validated english: Therefore, it is the responsibility of the citizens and the government of Kenya to improve and protect infrastructure in order to advance effectively in that sector.

lusoga: Twabona endhovu mukaaga nga dhirikulya amakoola ku muti gwa Acacia, ogumanhikwa nga emere y'endhovu.

validated english: Our bus passed close to those elephants and one young elephant came near our bus and touched it.
lusoga: Bbaasi yaife yabitira kumpi n'enjovu edho era endala ku dho yaidha kumpi ni bbaasi yaife yaagikwataku.

validated english: I was able to stretch out my hand and touch its body.
lusoga: Nasobola okugolola omukono gwange ne ngema omubiri gwaagwo.

validated english: We were able to take pictures while it was nearby and eventually that elephant went back to join the other elephants. As we moved a little further ahead, we encountered many antelopes.
lusoga: Twaghanga okukuba ebifananie nga kiri kumpi era mu nkomerero enjovu eyo yairayo yeyunga ku dhindi.

validated english: Very many that were eating grass.
lusoga: Kamaala abaali balikulya eisubi.

validated english: Suddenly!
lusoga: Mangu inho!

validated english: A lion appeared that had been hiding in the tall grass and was seen hunting an antelope.
lusoga: Empologoma yaliwo nga yali yeekwese mu busubi obuleeyi era baagibona ng'eyigga akayana.

validated english: Before long, the antelopes sensed danger and began to run, scattering without knowing where they were going.
lusoga: Mu kaseera akatono, enkula dhaawulira akabi era dhaatoolera okulumuka, nga dhiyawukana nga tidhiidhi ghaali kujja.

validated english: That is when the lion appeared and began to chase them.
lusoga: Agho n'agho empologoma yaidha yaatoolera okubagoba.

validated english: That lion was large and had a lot of brown hair on its head and all over its body.
lusoga: Empologoma eyo yali nnene era yali nenviiri edhikiragala kamaala ku mutwe gwayo n'omubiri gwayo gwonagwona.

validated english: He was able to run fast but the antelope was not defeated, it ran like lightning to save its life.
lusoga: Yaghanga okulumuka mangu aye embogo tiyaghangula, yulumuka nga kikunta okuwonia obulamu bwayo.

validated english: But after all, he could not escape death and the lion caught him.
lusoga: Aye mu nkomerero, tiyaghanga kusimattuka kufa era empologoma yamugema.

validated english: Truly, there is no beginning without an end.
lusoga: Bwenebwene, tighaba ntandikwa awazira nkomerero.

validated english: We all witnessed that event with our own eyes.
lusoga: Twena twena twabona ekyo n'amaiso gaife.

validated english: For some students, it was the first time seeing a lion.
lusoga: Eri abasomi abandi, guno gwali mulundi gwaibwe ogusooka okubona empologoma.

validated english: What we witnessed made us fear the lion even more.
lusoga: Kye twabona kyatuleetera okutya empologoma ekiwulagho.

validated english: Besides that, there were fascinating animals with long necks; no one can fail to recognise a giraffe.
lusoga: Ng'oggyeeko ekyo, waaligho ebisolo ebisikiriza ebyali n'emikira emiwanvu; ghazira atayinza kulemererwa kumanha girafu.

validated english: They were eating leaves from the parasol tree.
lusoga: Baali balya makoola kuva ku muti gwa parasol.

validated english: After the lion had filled its stomach, we saw two hyenas circling around it waiting for leftovers.
lusoga: Empologoma bweyamala okwidhuza olubuto, twabona enkembo ibiri nga dhigyetoloire nga dhirinda ebyasigalira.

validated english: As soon as the lion left, they devoured the remaining carcasses greedily.
lusoga: Mpologoma bweyavaawo, baalya emirambo egisigaire mu mululu.

validated english: That is when I came to believe the saying, greedy as a hyena.
lusoga: Era n'ekiseera kye nafuniramu okwikiriza enkola ey'okuba omuluvu oti n'ogwa empologoma.

validated english: A little further ahead, we encountered three buffaloes and two rhinos that were grazing.
lusoga: Twagya nga tuli mu maiso katono, twabona ente dha nte dha mu nsiko isatu n'embogo ibiri nga dhirikulya.

validated english: I made sure to take pictures of all the animals I saw.
lusoga: Nakakasa okukuba ebifananie byebisolo byona byona byenabona.

validated english: By three o'clock, our stomachs began to rumble and complain of hunger.
lusoga: Ku saawa mwenda edh'omusana, endhala yatutandiikiriza okutulumira.

validated english: We were taken to a hotel located right inside the park.
lusoga: Baatutwaala mu wuteri eri munda mwirindiro lyebisolo.

validated english: There we met different tourists from different countries.
lusoga: Twagananayo abalambuuzi okuva mu maghanga agendhaghulo.

validated english: We talked to them and interacted with them well.
lusoga: Twabakubye ebidhuubo era twakolagaine nabo bukalamu.

validated english: While we were in the middle of our conversation, one of the tourists stood up and
lusoga: Bwe twali mu kaseera akokwogera, owundi ku balambuuzi yaasituka yaakoba ati,

validated english: to introduce himself in English as James Bon from Japan and that whoever answers his question will receive a prize.
lusoga: okwetembeeta mu Lungereza nga James Bon okuva e Japan era nti buli alikwanukula ekibuuzo kye alifuna ekirabo.

validated english: He asked whoever could tell him the title of his book that was released last month.
lusoga: Yabuuza buli muntu eyali asobola okumukobera ekitiibwa ky'ekitabo kye ekyasibulwa omwezi ogubise.

validated english: Since I loved reading storybooks, I found myself raising my hand and the answer slipped out before I was given permission to respond.
lusoga: Olwokuba nali ngonza okusoma ebitabo by'enfumo, nesanga nga nseetula omukono era ekyokwiramu kyavaayo nga bakaali na kumpa lukusa kwanukula.

validated english: He took something out of the bag he had and told me that I had gotten it right.
lusoga: Yatoola ekintu mu nsagho yaakoba nti nali nkiidhi.

validated english: Upon opening that small box, I found every kind of his books that I had longed to read.
lusoga: Bwe naggulawo akasanduuko ako, nayagaana buli kika kya bitabo bye nali nenda okusoma.

validated english: Out of joy for receiving those books, I hugged him.
lusoga: Olw'okuba nali musanhufu olw'okufuna ebitabo ebyo, namugwa mu kifuba.

validated english: After that, we bid farewell and set off on the journey back.
lusoga: Twamala twasiibula era twasimbula okwira.

validated english: Before leaving the park, we passed a pond full of hippos and beside that pond we saw a crocodile with its mouth open, showing it was full.
lusoga: Nga tukaali kuva mu kifo ekyo, twabita ku kidiba ekyali kijjudde embiidhi era ku luuyi olundi olw'ekidiba ekyo twabona goonya ng'omunwa gwayo gugwire, nga kiraga nti yali eidhwire.

validated english: The return journey was short because most of us were tired.
lusoga: Olugendo olwokwira lwali luwulawo kuba abasinga bungi ku ife twali tukooye.

validated english: When I got home, I narrated everything that had happened to my parents without leaving out a single detail.
lusoga: Bwe natuuka eka, nayogera buli kintu ekyali kibairegho eri abazaire bange nga tireseire kintu kyonakyona.

validated english: Finally, they informed me that they had received a call from President Uhuru, asking me to give him a report of what had happened.
lusoga: Oluvainhuma, baakobera bati baali bafunie okwogera okuva ewa omukulembeze weighanga Uhuru, ng'ansaba okumuwa alipoota ku byali bibairegho.

validated english: When I finished, I got ready to sleep at 9:45 PM.
lusoga: Bwe namaliriza, neetegeka okwebaka ku saawa mwenda n'ekitundu edh'ekyegulo.

validated english: As I lay on the bed, I exhaled deeply and in that moment, I truly believed that day had been a remarkably wonderful one.
lusoga: Bwe nali nga ndhigala ku buliri, nafuuwa omukka mu bwidhuvu era mu kaseera ako, nali nkiriza nti olunaku lwali lwa kitalo.

validated english: UNFORGETTABLE MOMENTS Yes!
lusoga: Ebiseera ebitayinza kwerabirwa!

validated english: Events that seem impossible or take a very long time to materialize will eventually occur.
lusoga: Ebigwa bitalaze ebyo ebirabika nga tibisoboka oba ebitwala akabanga akawanvu okutuukirira biri n'okubaagho.

validated english: The moment I had been eagerly and excitedly waiting for arrived.
lusoga: Ekiseera kye nali ntegeike okuba nakyo kyatuuka.

validated english: I woke up as the world lifted its black cloak, ready to welcome Mr Sun to take charge.
lusoga: Nazuukuka ng'ensi erikusitula ekizibaala kyayo ekyobwirugavu, nga yetegeike okusangaaza omwami enkyo okutwala obuvunanizibwa.

validated english: The dew on the grass shimmered brightly as it danced gently like diamonds to welcome the day.
lusoga: Omugoye ku bimuli gwali gwaka ng'oti dhi dayimanda nga gusagamba okusangaaza olunaku.

validated english: And the sweet voices of the birds singing their songs filled the air.
lusoga: Eiroboozi ery'ebinhonhi ebirikwemba lyaidhwire empewo.

validated english: Indeed, a good day is seen in the morning.
lusoga: Bwenebwene, olunaku olukalamu balulabira mu kunkyo.

validated english: I prepared carefully because that day I had unmatched excitement.
lusoga: Nategeka n'obwegendereza kuba olunaku olwo nali n'ebisobyo.

validated english: A short while later, I was at the table having breakfast.
lusoga: Nga ghabiseegho akaseera katono, nali ku meeza nga ndya eky'ekyankyo.

validated english: Afterward, I carried water, a pen, a book and a camera.
lusoga: Nga nva agho, natwala amaadhi, akafumo, ekitabo n'ekyuma eky'okukuba ebifananie.

validated english: Before leaving for school, my mother gave me money for that day's expenses because it was the eve of a trip to Tsavo East National Park.
lusoga: Nga tiniinie kuja kwisomero, maama yampa empiiya edhokukozesa ku lunaku olwo kuba lwali lunaku lwa kusimbula kuja mu kifo kya kusimba nsolo ekye Tsavo East National Park.

validated english: After a while, I left home and headed to school.
lusoga: Nga ghabiseegho akaseera, naleka eka naaja kwisomero.

validated english: At the edge of the path, I could see the station.
lusoga: Kunkomerero y'oluguudo, nali nsobola okubona ekifo awasimbwa.

validated english: Believe it or not, my face shone with joy and pure delight.
lusoga: Kikusobeku oba tosobeku, omumwa gwange gwali gwaka n'eisanhu.

validated english: I quickened my pace so I could arrive faster.
lusoga: Nayongeza ku misinde gyange nsobole okutuuka amangu.

validated english: A short while later, the bus arrived at the station and finally I got inside.
lusoga: Nga ghabiseegho akaseera katono, bbaasi yatuuka ku siteegi era naasembayo okugingiramu.

validated english: When the conductor had loaded some of the other passengers' luggage, he jumped in and we set off.
lusoga: Omugemagani bweyali aghanze okutikka ebitereke eby'abandi, yasimbula twafuluma.

validated english: When I arrived at school, everyone was overflowing with joy, like a toothless person who had just grown teeth.
lusoga: Bwe natuuka kwisomero, buli muntu yali musangaavu, oti n'omuntu azira maino aghozaala amaino.

validated english: Everyone arrived early.
lusoga: Buli muntu yatuuse kikerezi.

validated english: Before our journey began, the head teacher, Mrs. Kidala, appointed me as the class prefect.
lusoga: Ng'olugendo lwaife lukaali kwinhama, omukulu weisomero, Mukyala Kidala, yantongoza okuba omukulu wekibiina.

validated english: Something I had never given much thought to, for this was a great honor to me.
lusoga: Ekintu kye nali tinhanga kudhuuba kinhwevu, kuba kano kaali kitiibwa kya maani ye nze.

validated english: Without delay, the bus arrived and we wasted no time boarding it.
lusoga: Awazira kulwa, bbaasi yatuuka era titwakozesa kiseera kigere kugirinngamu.

validated english: My friend and I
lusoga: Nze ni Mukwano gwange.

validated english: Fortunately, we got seats near the window.
lusoga: Ekyomukisa, twafuna ebifo kumpi n'endhigi.

validated english: After everyone had boarded and found a place to sit.
lusoga: Buli muntu bweyamala okwetantala era nafuna ekifo aghokutyama.

validated english: I led the travel prayer because a journey begins with a step and a traveller at the coast.
lusoga: Nakulemberera okusaba okwokutambula kuba olugendo lutandikira ku mutendera n'omutambuze ku mwalo.

validated english: As soon as the journey began, the commotion started because some of the travellers chatted, others admired the scenery and others were singing.
lusoga: Olugendo bwe lwainhama, akavuyo kaatoolera kuba abandi ku basabaze baali balikunhuma, abandi nga bali kwerolera ebintu ebiri mu maaso, ate abandi nga bayemba.

validated english: Moreover, the music playing in the bus captivated us completely.
lusoga: Ate era, enhembo edhiri kusindikibwa mu bbaasi dhaatugema inho.

validated english: From the outside, you would think they were Christians overwhelmed by the abundance of the Holy Spirit.
lusoga: Okuva ku luya, wadhuuba oti baali Bakulisitayo abaali baidhwire Mwoyo Mutukuvu.

validated english: In the blink of an eye, we passed a place that had a large crowd of people.
lusoga: Mu kaseera katono, twabita mu kifo aghaali abantu kamaala.

validated english: When I asked our teacher, she told us that it was Heroes Day and those people were waiting for the president to address them.
lusoga: Bwe nabuuza omusomesa waife, yatukoba ati lwaali lunaku lwa bazira era abantu abo baali balindirira mukulembeze waighanga abakobere.

validated english: Just as we moved a little further.
lusoga: Bwe twatambula katono.

validated english: Our bus came face to face with the president's car.
lusoga: Bbaasi yaife yaidhira maiso ku maiso n'emotoka ya mukulembeze waighanga.

validated english: President Uhuru alighted and our teachers went to welcome him.
lusoga: Omukulembeze weighanga Uhuru yavaamu era abasomesa baife baaja okumusangaaza.

validated english: After a brief conversation, I was appointed by the head teacher to welcome the president and introduce him to my fellow trainees.
lusoga: Olumalirira lw'okunhwa ku mboozi, mukulu weisomero yantuma okusangaaza omukulembeze weighanga n'okumwanjulira abandi be twali tuli kwetendeka nabo.

validated english: Believe it or not, the president gave me numerous compliments and eventually ordered the festival to begin.
lusoga: Kikukakataku oba toikukakataku, omukulembeze weighanga yampa ebisembo kamaala era yasalagho nti ekikuudhuko kitandike.

validated english: People began dancing while others were eating.
lusoga: Abantu baatoolera okukina ate abandi baali balya.

validated english: After a while, silence fell as everyone waited for the president's speech.
lusoga: Olumalirira lwakabanga, eisirifu lyagwa nga buli muntu alindirira endhogera ya mukulembeze waighanga.

validated english: After that speech, we all went to bid farewell to the president and continued with our tour.
lusoga: Olumalirira lw'endhogera eyo, twenatwena twaja okusiibula omukulembeze weighanga era twasigala nga tutalaaga.

validated english: After a while, we saw animals such as antelopes, wild dogs and many others grazing while others were searching for food.
lusoga: Nga ghabiseegho akabanga, twabona ebisolo nga entalagire, embwa edh'omunsiko n'ebindi kamaala nga birikulya ate ebindi nga birikunoonia emere.

validated english: I took out my camera and took their videos and pictures.
lusoga: Naghaayo kamera yange neekuba ebifaananie bya vidiyo dhaibwe.

validated english: Suddenly, a lion appeared, hiding in the grass, looking for prey.
lusoga: Mangu ago, empologoma yaidha, ng'ekweka mu bisubi, ng'enoonya ekyokulya.

validated english: Trouble is no stranger, the antelopes sensed danger and began to run to save their lives, not knowing where they were heading.
lusoga: Obuzibu tibuli ghala, entale dhaawulira akabi era dhaatoolera okulumuka okuwonia obulamu bwaadho, nga tidhidhi ghaali dhija.

validated english: The lion did not want to be left behind either, so he chased them while roaring.
lusoga: Empologoma yena tiyayenda kulekebwa inyuma, kale yabayiiga ng'ewuluguma.

validated english: That lion was large and had thick brown hair on its head.
lusoga: Empologoma eyo yali nnene era yali nenviiri edhikwafu edhikwafu ku mutwe.

validated english: The antelope braced itself to run like lightning, but alas, it was all in vain.
lusoga: Ekiwuka kyetegekera okulumuka ng'oti luyengo, aye eky'omukisa omubi, byona byali bya bwereere.

validated english: His efforts bore no fruit as he could not escape death and thus he was caught.
lusoga: Amaanhi ge tigaavaamu kuba yali tasobola kubulawo kufa era baamugema.

validated english: We were all filled with fear as we witnessed how the lion killed the antelope.
lusoga: Twaidhwire okutya nga twalingirira empologoma nga yeyita enkula.

validated english: Truly, there is no beginning without an end.
lusoga: Bwenebwene, tigha ntandikwa awazira nkomerero.

validated english: Oh! It was a truly terrifying event.
lusoga: Oh! Kyali kintu kya kutya inho.

validated english: However, we saw many hyenas surrounding the lion waiting to eat the remains of the antelope.
lusoga: Aye twabona emisege kamaala nga gizungirire empologoma nga girinda kulya ebyasigaire ku mbiidhi.

validated english: When the lion left, they devoured the carcass greedily.
lusoga: Empologoma bweyavaagho, baalya omulambo n'omululu.

validated english: After three hours, we docked at Tsavo wildlife park.
lusoga: Oluvainhuma lwa saawa isatu, twatuuka ku kifo eky'ebisolo byomunsiko ekye Tsavo.

validated english: The joy we had was unparalleled.
lusoga: Eisanhu lye twabaire nalyo tiryali na kigera.

validated english: We entered with joy and jubilation.
lusoga: Twangira n'okusanhusa n'okwesuuta.

validated english: One of the park rangers told us that he would be the one to guide us and also informed us of the rules we were required to observe while inside the park.
lusoga: Omulala ku balabirira eikumiro yatukobera ati n'eyali ow'okutulambuza era yatukobera amateeka ge twali tuli n'okugondera nga tuli munda mw'eikumiro.

validated english: Among those rules are not littering and not making noise.
lusoga: Mu biragiro ebyo mulimu obutasuulasuula kasasiro n'obutakola buleekaana.

validated english: After that, we entered the park and the first animals we saw were monkeys. Those monkeys were on a baobab tree, with some eating forest fruits and others jumping from one tree to another.
lusoga: Twamala twingira mu kifo awakuumirwa ebisolo era ebisolo ebyasooka okuboneka byali mawuulu. Amawuulu ago gaali ku muti gwa baobab, agandi nga galya bibala bya mu kibira ate agandi nga gakubuuka okuva ku muti okujja ku gundi.

validated english: As we continued walking, we saw an animal called a mongoose that was eating a large snake it had caught.
lusoga: Bwe twali tuli kugenda, twabona ekisolo ekikalamu nga kiri kulya omusota omunene gwekyali kigemye.

validated english: Beside where he was, there was a small hole from which a fat cane rat emerged.
lusoga: Nga okuva aghaali, waaligho ekiina ekitono omukira omunene mwe gwava.

validated english: Not far from there was a bird called zurakulu that was pecking at insects.
lusoga: Tiyali ghala agho ghaaligho ekinyonyi ekya zurakulu nga kiri kusima biswa.

validated english: The more we continued walking in the park, the more we saw various animals and trees such as baobabs and wild banana trees.
lusoga: Bwe tweyongera okutambula mu kifo ekisirifu, twabona ebisolo ebyendhaghulo n'emiti nga baababu n'emiti gy'amatooke ag'omunsiko.

validated english: They were quite large indeed.
lusoga: Dhaali dha maani inho.

validated english: I arrived home eager to narrate to my grandparents all that had happened during the trip.
lusoga: Natuuka eka nga ndi musuubuzi okukobera dhaadha wange ne dhaadha omukazi byonabyona ebyali bibairegho mu lugendo.

validated english: Truly, it was a very splendid day in my life.
lusoga: Mu butuufu, lwali lunaku lwa kitiisa mu bulamu bwange.

validated english: IMPORTANCE OF INFRASTRUCTURE IN KENYA It is evidently clear that infrastructure is a fundamental tool in the economic development of a country.
lusoga: OMUGASO GW'EBINTU EBISOBOSA EBYENFUNA MU KENYA Kiboneka bukalamu nti eby'okukozesa mu byenfuna bya mugaso mu byenkulankulana y'ebyenfuna byeighanga.

validated english: Infrastructure is also known to be an important component in development needs.
lusoga: Eby'okukozesa mu by'entambula byoona byoona byamakulu mu byetaago by'enkulankulana.

validated english: Infrastructure does not directly produce goods, but it helps in flourishing, thriving and strengthening production.
lusoga: Eby'okukozesa tibivaamu byamaguzi buterevu, aye biyamba mu kweyongera, okukula n'okunhweza eby'okukola.

validated english: Infrastructure is an important component in development needs.
lusoga: Eby'okukozesa mu by'okukulankulania byamakulu mu byetaago by'okukulankulania.

validated english: It can manifest in two branches.
lusoga: Kisobola okweyoleka mu matabi abiri.

validated english: These include visible and tangible infrastructure such as traffic lights, sewage drainage systems, bridges, electricity pylons, water systems and airport runways.
lusoga: Muno mulimu ebintu ebirabwaku nga ebitaala bya kunguudo, emifulejje gy'empita-mbiidhi, entindo, ebikondo by'amasanhalaze, emifulejje gy'amadhi n'ebisaawe by'enhonhi.

validated english: It also emerges in an intangible branch which includes the knowledge required to maintain infrastructure including the internet system.
lusoga: Kino era kiboneka mu kintu ekizira kubonera na maiso omuli amagezi agetaagisa okukuuma ebyokukozesa omuli n'omutimbagano.

validated english: Infrastructure is very important, especially in production and development in the country.
lusoga: Eby'okukozesa byamakulu inho, namunswa mu by'okutuusa ebyamaguzi ku katale n'okukulankulana mu byenfuna byeighanga.

validated english: Some of its significance is as follows.
lusoga: Ebindi ku bikulu byaakyo biri bityo.

validated english: It helps to enhance security.
lusoga: Kiyamba okutumbula ebyokwerinda.

validated english: Security will be greatly stable because all roads will be passable due to the absence of potholes.
lusoga: Ebyokwerinda biidha kuba birungi kuba enguudo dhoona dhoona dhiidha kuba dhirikusoboka olwobutaba na binnya.

validated english: They will be perfectly straight!
lusoga: Baidha kuba baterevu!

validated english: It brings development due to the absence of accidents, meaning that the government will not incur losses or financial shortages in purchasing medicine and meeting the needs of patients affected by road accidents.
lusoga: Kireeta enkulankulana olwobutaba na bubendhe, ekitegeeza nti gavumenti teidha kufiirwa oba kubulwa byakukozesa mu kugula obulezi n'okutuukiriza ebyetaago by'abalwaire abakoseibwa obubendhe bw'okunguudo.

validated english: The country's budget will also not be affected by activities resulting from road accidents.
lusoga: Ebyembalirira byeighanga byoona tibidha kukosebwa mirimo egiva ku bubendhe bwa kunguudo.

validated english: In addition to that, it can help in the production of energy that can be used in industries to support and promote various products.
lusoga: Okwongereza ku ekyo, kisobola okuyamba mu kukola amasanhalaze agasobola okukozesebwa mu makolero okuwagira n'okutumbula ebyamaguzi ebyendhaghulo.

validated english: Energy is needed in various types of industries to assist in the production of goods.
lusoga: Amasanhalaze geetaagisa mu makolero agendhaghulo okuyamba mu kukola ebyamaguzi.

validated english: Energy, such as electricity, is highly needed because it brings considerable benefits to our lives.
lusoga: Amasanhalaze, nga amasaanhalaze g'omunhumba, getagisa inho kuba galeeta emiganhulo kamaala mu bulamu bwaife.

validated english: It helps with lighting to carry out and implement various tasks such as aiding in the ownership of our homes to enable seeing.

lusoga: Obubendhe kamaala mu Kenya obuva ku mwenge.

validated english: Many drivers use alcohol and drugs especially mogokaa and miraa as an excuse to be able to drive for long hours.
lusoga: Abavuzi kamaala abakozesa omwenge n'ebirezirezi okusingira irala omwenge gwa Mogoka n'omwenge gwa Miraa okuba ekyekwasa okusobola okuvuga okumala esaawa edhighanvu.

validated english: Alcohol drinkers claim that it helps them not to feel tired and even to enjoy themselves while driving.
lusoga: Abanhwi ba mwenge bakoba bati kibayamba obutawulira bakooye ate na kweyagala nga bavuga.

validated english: According to statistics, five thousand people since the year 2020 have bid the world farewell
lusoga: Okusinzira ku bibalo, abantu omutwalo mulamba bukya omwaka 2020 gutandika bafudde.

validated english: due to drunk drivers.

validated english: This problem can be solved by setting up checkpoints every few kilometres, especially at night when drunk drivers struggle to make decisions, particularly when faced with situations that require sudden judgement, for example, an animal crossing in front of the vehicle.
lusoga: Ekizibu kino basobola okukigonhoola nga bategeka ebifo byokukebereramu buli luvainhuma lwa kilomita ntono, okusingira irala mu bwire abavuzi abatamiivu webakalubirirwa okusalagho, okusingira irala bwebaba bali mu mbeera edhetaagisa okusalagho amangu, okugeza, ekisolo okusala mu maiso g'ekimotoka.

validated english: The fourth issue is that roads have lacked maintenance.
lusoga: Ensonga eyokuna eri nti enguudo tidhiri kudhikirabiriza.

validated english: and being in a dissatisfactory state.

validated english: Roads are impassable especially dirt roads during the rainy season.
lusoga: Enguudo tidhbitikamu naddala enguudo edh'omukyangaala mu biseera byamaadhi.

validated english: Friday, October 20, 2006 I attended the Kenyatta Day celebrations at Nyayo Stadium.
lusoga: Olwokutaanu, Okitoba 20, 2006 nali ku bikudhuko bya Kenyatta ku kisaawe kya Nyayo.

validated english: It was a splendid celebration although the sun scorched intensely.
lusoga: Kyabaire kikudhuko kikalamu waire ng'endhuba yali ekaliire inho.

validated english: I met Stella, my childhood friend, after the celebration.
lusoga: Nasanga Stella, mukwano gwange okuva mu buto, olumalirira lw'ekikuudhuko.

validated english: Saturday, October 21, 2006 I picked up my suit from the dry cleaner and later went swimming and relaxed at the beach.
lusoga: Olwomukaaga, Okitobba 21, 2006 nafuna suuti yange okuva mu kifo webagikubira era naaja okuwuga naawuumula ku lubalama.

validated english: Sunday, October 22, 2006 I woke up very late.

validated english: Interview An interview is a situation where a person or people are asked questions by an individual or a group of people and the answers they give.
lusoga: Okubuuza ebibuuzo embeera omuntu oba abantu ababuuza ebibuuzo omuntu oba abantu abandi era n'eby'okwiramu byebawa.

validated english: It has specific characteristics: I. It has a specific purpose. II.
lusoga: Kiri n'ebintu ebyawukana: I. Kiri n'ekigendererwa ekyawukana. II.

validated english: It follows a specific procedure. III.
lusoga: Kigema ku nkola eyendhaghulo.

validated english: Time, place, its duration, participants and the topic/issue to be discussed are usually specified before the activity itself.
lusoga: Ekiseera, ekifo, ekiseera kyakimala, abantu abalikwenhigiramu n'ensonga yebalikwogeraku batera okubikoba nga bakaali na kukola kintu.

validated english: One group of participants usually controls the conversation and mainly asks questions while the other largely provides answers.
lusoga: Ekibindha ekyabantu abenhigiremu batera okufuga ebyokwogera era batera okubuuza ebibuuzo ate abandi batera kwanukula.

validated english: Participants in these groups usually do not have relational equality.
lusoga: Abantu abali mu bibindha bino tibatera kuba na bwenkania.

validated english: In an interview there is the interviewer and also the interviewee.
lusoga: Mu kubuuzibwa waliwo ababuuza n'abo bebabuuza.

validated english: There was a shortage of leafy vegetables and fruits.
lusoga: Waaliwo eikekwa ly'enva endiirwa n'ebibala.

validated english: The interviewer may ask questions or make statements that prompt the interviewee to provide explanations or clarifications about the subject matter.
lusoga: Omubuuzi asobola okubuuza ebibuuzo oba okukola ebyogerwa ebireetera omubuuzibwa okuwaayo okunhonhola oba okulambulula ku nsonga.

validated english: Interviews can be brief and spontaneous or long and prearranged.
lusoga: Okubuuza ebibuuzo kusobola okuba okumpimpi ate nga kwa mangu oba okuwanvu ate nga kutegekeibwa.

validated english: An example of a spontaneous interview is when you encounter a journalist, perhaps as you're leaving a meeting or while on a walk, and they ask you questions right then and there.
lusoga: Ekyokuboneraku ekyokubuuza okuva mu mbeera n'okwagaana omunamakobo, oba nga oli kulekawo olwekobaano oba nga oli ku lugendo, era baakubuuza ebibuuzo mu kaseera ako.

validated english: Planned interviews are those conducted after the interviewee has been informed in advance and has prepared specifically for the purpose of being interviewed.
lusoga: Okubuuzibwa okw'entegeka n'okwo okukolebwa olumalirira lw'okukobera omuntu nti balikumubuuza era nga yeesuubira.

validated english: This type of interview addresses the issue in depth.
lusoga: Ekika kyebibuuzo kino kigema kunsonga mu bwidhuvu.

validated english: Purpose of interviews There are many types of interviews each with a specific purpose or several roles.
lusoga: Omugaso gwokubuuza ebibuuzo Waliwo ebika byokubuuza ebibuuzo kamaala nga buli kika kiri n'omugaso gwaakyo oba emirimo kamaala.

validated english: a. To explain and convey information There are interviews whose purpose is to inform people and explain an issue. To defend a certain position There are interviews where people from two sides with differing views on a particular issue may be interviewed and each gets a chance to defend the perspective they support.
lusoga: a. Okusobola okulambulula n'okutuusa obubaka Waliwo okubuuza ebibuuzo nga ekigendererwa kya kusomesa bantu na kulambulula ensonga. Okulwanirira endhuuba eyindi Waliwo okubuuza ebibuuzo abantu okuva ku mbali dhombiriri abali n'endhuuba edhendhaghulo ku nsonga eyindi webabuuza era buli muntu afuna omukisa okulwanirira endhuuba yebawagira.

validated english: c. To investigate an issue or a person. Interviews can aim to investigate an issue or a person in depth. For example, a person's life or actions etc. can be examined. Additionally, an issue can be explored broadly such as why acts of terrorism are carried out.
lusoga: c. Okunoonereza ku nsonga oba omuntu. Okubuuza ebibuuzo kusobola okuba n'ekigendererwa eky'okunoonereza ku nsonga oba omuntu mu bwidhuvu. Okugeza, obulamu bw'omuntu oba ebikolwa bye n'ebirala bisobola okwekebejjebwa. Okwongereza ku ekyo, ensonga esobola okwekebejjebwa mu bwidhuvu nga lwaki ebikolwa bya butujju bikolebwa.

validated english: d. Entertainment. Some interviews are aimed solely at entertaining. For example, a certain artist may be invited for an interview with the intention of entertaining the audience.
lusoga: d. Ebyamasanhu. Okubuuzibwa okundi kugendereire kusanhusa. Okugeza, omwembi omulala asobola okwetebwa mu kubuuzibwa n'ekigendererwa ekyokusanhusa abantu.

validated english: These various roles may emerge in interviews although many interviews incorporate several roles in their execution.
lusoga: Emirimo gino egyendhaghulo gisobola okuvaayo mu kubuuzibwa ebibuuzo waire nga okubuuzibwa ebibuuzo kuno kuyinza okubaamu emirimo kamaala mu kugikola.

validated english: Media interviews There are things that can help the interviewer and the interviewee to make the interview successful.
lusoga: Okubuuza ebibuuzo mu banamakobo Waliwo ebintu ebiyamba omubuuza n'omubuuzibwa okukola okubuuza okukalamu.

validated english: We will discuss those matters.
lusoga: Tujja kukubagania ebidhuubo ku nsonga edho.

validated english: How the interviewer can make the interview successful One important thing for a journalist is to prepare by researching the issue they intend to interview someone about.
lusoga: Engeri omubuuzi w'ebibuuzo y'asobola okukola okubuuzibwa okukalamu Ekintu ekikulu eri omunamakobo kutegeka nga noonereza ku nsonga y'oyenda okubuuza omuntu.

validated english: This will enable them to gain more knowledge about the topic they are focusing on and thus help them prepare appropriate questions to ask the interviewee and also provide direction for the conversation during the interview.
lusoga: Kino kibayamba okufuna amagezi agawulagho ku nsonga yebalikukola era kyabayamba okutegeka ebibuuzo ebituufu ebyokubuuza ababuuzi era n'okubagha obulagirizi ku byebalikwogera mu kiseera kyokubuuza.

validated english: Moreover, good choice of words during an interview is important.
lusoga: Ate era, okulonda obukalamu ebigambo mu kiseera kyokubuuzibwa kya makulu.

validated english: Simple language without ambiguous statements is appropriate.
lusoga: Olulimi olwangu nga luziramu kubuzabuza lusaanira.

validated english: You need to prepare the questions you will ask but do not rely on them during the interview.
lusoga: Kikwetaagisa okutegeka ebibuuzo by'oidha okubuuza aye tobyesigamaku mu kubuuzibwa.

validated english: It is not necessary to follow them.
lusoga: Ti kya makulu kubigondera.

validated english: You also need to ask questions that come to mind during the interview.
lusoga: Oli n'okubuuza ebibuuzo ebikujira mu bwongo mu kiseera ky'okubuuzibwa ebibuuzo.

validated english: Listen carefully to the answers you are given and analyse the points to identify new emerging arguments.
lusoga: Wuliriza bukalamu ebyokwanukula byebakuwa era weetegereze ensonga okuzuula ensonga empyaka edhirikubalukagho.

validated english: Media interviews require the questions asked to be investigative and perhaps challenging to the interviewee as well as simple and enjoyable.
lusoga: Okubuuza ebibuuzo mu banamakobo kwetagisa ebibuuzo ebibuuzibwa okuba nga bya kunoonereza era nga biyinza okuba nga bikalubu eri ababuuzibwa era nga byangu era nga bisanhusa.

validated english: Your interviews will be balanced by doing this.
lusoga: Okubuuzibwa kwo kujja kuba kwa mwenkanonkano nga okoze kino.

validated english: When you begin the interview, go straight to the point.
lusoga: Bwotandika okubuuza ebibuuzo,ja butereevu ku nsonga.

validated english: The interviewee needs to be given the opportunity to speak without delay.
lusoga: Omubuuzi ali n'okugheebwa omukisa okwogera awazira kulwa.

validated english: A simple and brief answer requires k right at the beginning.
lusoga: Ekyokwanukula ekyangu era ekyamangu kyetaagisa kuba kituufu ku ntandikwa.

validated english: For example, where were you born?
lusoga: Ng'ekyokuboneraku, wazaalibwa wa?

validated english: Then follow up with the question you prefer most or the one you consider more important.
lusoga: Agho oidhukira ekibuuzo kyoyenda oba kyodhuuba nti kya makulu.

validated english: There may not be enough time to answer even important questions later.
lusoga: Wayinza okubulawo ekiseera ekimala okwanukula ebibuuzo ebikulu eby'oluvainhuma.

validated english: Try to be calm and patient throughout the interview.
lusoga: Gezaaku okuba omukkakkamu era omuguminkiriza mu kiseera ky'okubuuzibwa ebibuuzo.

validated english: The person you are interviewing might evade the question you asked several times but you will need to maintain your calm and ask it again.
lusoga: Omuntu gwolikubuuza ayinza okwewala ekibuuzo kyewabuuziza emikuzi kamaala aye olikwetagisa okusigala nga oli mukkakkamu era olikwetagisa okukibuuza kabiri.

validated english: Always be courteous before and during the interview.
lusoga: Beera wa mpisa buli kiseera nga bakaali na mu kiseera kyokubuuzibwa ebibuuzo.

validated english: You can maintain a smile and also ensure that you appear to understand and be in control of the topic being discussed.
lusoga: Osobola okusigala ng'oliku akamwenhu era okakasa nti olikutegeera era oli mu buyinza ku nsonga erikukubaganiibwaku ebidhuubo.

validated english: Show that you are interested in the matter you are investigating.
lusoga: Laga nti olikwenda okumanha kunsonga yooli kunoonereza.

validated english: It is important to show that you genuinely need the information you are seeking.
lusoga: Kya makulu okulaga nti wenda amagezi g'obuuza.

validated english: Ensure that your voice is clearly audible and pleasant.
lusoga: Kakasa nti amamiro go gawulikika bukalamu era nga gali malungi.

validated english: Along with this, if it is television, smart clothing is appropriate.
lusoga: Ng'ogaitiireku kino, bwekiba terefayina, engoye edh'amagezi dhituukaana.

validated english: The interviewer must have a clear mind, be quick to understand things and also have a broad general knowledge.
lusoga: Omubuuzi ali n'okuba n'endhuuba enkalamu, okutegeera ebintu mangu ate n'okuba n'amagezi agawera.

validated english: Radio Interviews Apart from the matters discussed above, remember that radio interviews rely heavily on voice.
lusoga: Okubuuza ebibuuzo ku ladiyo Okwongereza ku nsonga edhigemagana ku ghaigulu, dhiidhukire nti okubuuza ebibuuzo ku ladiyo kyesigama inho ku mboozi.

validated english: Therefore body gestures do not help you in your interviewing activity.
lusoga: N'olw'ekyo ebikolwa by'omubiri tibikuyamba mu bya kubuuza bibuuzo.

validated english: Your language should be appealing and persuasive.
lusoga: Olulimi lwo luli n'okuba nga lusikiriza era nga lusendasenda.

validated english: Choose your words carefully and do not use technical or controversial vocabulary.
lusoga: Londa ebibono byo n'obwegendereza era tokozesa bibono bya bya tekinologiya oba ebyokulwanagana.

validated english: The voice must also be pleasant.
lusoga: Eiroboozi lirinokuba nga lisikiriza.
